pageCache.pageTitle: St Mark's CE Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Together, in God’s love, we will shine
HEADTEACHER'S WELCOME
Welcome to St. Mark's CE Primary School! We hope you will find all the information you need on these pages, but please do get in touch with us if we can help at all or if you would like a tour of our lovely little school.
We are now showing people around for children due to start school in September 2027 - if you would like to book an appointment, please contact the school office on 01444 400398 or office@st-marks.w-sussex.sch.uk
Laura Kelsey, Headteacher
WHAT MAKES US SPECIAL
At St Mark’s CE Primary School we aim to provide a Christian environment where everyone feels valued, respected and secure. Our curriculum is rich, challenging and inclusive and we aim to make learning lively, fun and active. We find that children respond very positively to the school’s caring ethos and atmosphere and benefit from pursuing a modern education in the traditional setting of a village school.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mark's CE Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
Welcome to the Governors' section.
School governors are people who want to make a positive contribution to children’s education. Governors are the largest volunteer force in the country and are accountable to West Sussex County Council, the Diocese of Chichester, and to you, the Parents & Carers of our pupils.
The Governors represent various groups within the school community: the parents, the church, the community and the staff. In addition to some statutory responsibilities, their role is three fold: setting the vision, ethos and strategic direction of the school, holding school leaders to account for the performance of pupils and the performance of staff and ensuring the school’s finances are well spent.
The Governors elect a Chair and Vice chair each year and it is their responsibility to run the meetings. Full governor meetings are held regularly and the various committees report to these meetings.
Most school issues are best addressed to the relevant class teacher or the Headteacher, but if there is something you would like to suggest or talk to us about, please write to the Governors via the school office. Please mark your letter 'Private'.
Mrs Judith Belham - Foundation Governor
Mrs Helen Arnold - Foundation Governor. Vice Chair, Chair of Staffing & Pay committee
Rev Carl Smith - Foundation
Ms Laura Kelsey - Headteacher
Mrs Kerri Potter - Parent Governor.
Chair of Resources Committee
Mrs Monique Mendes Da Costa

pageCache.pageTitle: St Mark's CE Primary School - Residential Trips
pageCache.text:
Residential Trips
After consultation with parents, we are now taking Laurel children on a residential to Windmill Hill PGL every other year. This means all children will attend a residential either in Year 5 or Year 6 when they are in Laurel class. The benefits of these visits are numerous and are a highlight of the children’s experience whilst at school. Not only do the children take part in activities we cannot provide at school, but they benefit by learning many skills that help with independence, leadership and organisation.
The cost varies from year to year but we will ensure that all children get the opportunity to enjoy this very valuable experience. If the cost should be a problem for parents we ask them to come into school and discuss this in the strictest confidence.
For more information:
https://www.pgl.co.uk/en-gb/school-trips/primary-schools/centres/windmill-hill
